history.summary: The Devka Sun Temple, dedicated to Surya, is a 12th-13th-century temple built in the Solanki/Gurjara-Pratihara architectural idiom, standing on a height in Devka village. It is known for its shikhara, intricate carvings and subsidiary shrines; Archaeological Department inscriptions recorded on columns are dated V.S. 1631 and V.S. 1674, and a conservation action plan has been proposed by the state government. The village also holds a Vishnu temple and the ruins of two other ancient temples with stone sculptures of Lord Ganesha. CSV town 'Barmer' must be corrected: the temple is NOT in Barmer city but in Devka, a hamlet about 62 km from Barmer along the Barmer-Jaisalmer road (12 km north of Sheo). Note there is a separate Balark Sun Temple at Juna Barmer -- do not conflate the two Sun shrines.

name: Devka-Sun Temple
town_description: Devka is a small hamlet in Sheo tehsil of Barmer district, about 62 km from Barmer city along the Barmer-Jaisalmer road (NH-15), 12 km north of Sheo; the desert landscape and a group of ancient shrines surround the Sun temple.
